promo-card-fold.title: Your folded card prints upside down #shorts
promo-card-fold.description:
Lay out a folded card the way it looks right on screen and the back prints upside down. Every time.

Fold a sheet in half and the top half flips over. The left panel does not stay where it is — it rotates 180 degrees and becomes the back of the card.

So anything on the left panel has to be placed upside down ON THE SHEET to come out the right way up ON THE CARD.

Your screen is a flat sheet. The card is a folded object. The card wins.

promo-card-inside.title: The inside of a folded card does NOT rotate #shorts
promo-card-inside.description:
This one catches people the other way. The outside left panel needs rotating. The inside does not.

Once folded, the inside reads as one landscape spread, left to right, exactly as it looks on screen. Only the panel that folds BEHIND changes its orientation.

One rotated panel. Outside. Left. That is the entire rule.

30-second test: scrap paper, write FRONT bottom-right and BACK bottom-left, fold it, look at where BACK ended up.

promo-card-score.title: Why your card cracks along the fold #shorts
promo-card-score.description:
Paper is layers of fibre. Bending it stretches the fibres on the outside of the curve, and if they cannot stretch, they tear — that is the white line through your fold.

Scoring crushes them in a controlled line first, so the fold has somewhere to happen.

Run the back of a butter knife, or a bone folder, down the centre against a ruler. Then fold against the score and run your thumbnail along it.

On ordinary paper you can skip it. On card stock you cannot.

promo-card-fourup.title: Full bleed from a printer that cannot do full bleed #shorts
promo-card-fourup.description:
Home printers have a border they physically cannot reach. So do not print to the edge — cut to it.

Four A6 card fronts on an A4 sheet, two by two. Each keeps its own 10 mm margin, but adjacent cards should touch on the shared line.

Cut down that line and both cards come out with colour right to the edge.

Steel rule and a sharp blade, three light passes. Scissors wander, and a wandering edge is what makes a card look homemade.
